newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 16.0/17.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 16.0/17.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta short-term money was expensive, with overnight money traded at 16.0/17.0 percent, but short-term swaps fell and overnight dollars rose, dealers said.
They said the current "anomaly" in the market was the result of recent turbulence in the foreign exchange market.
"But I think the condition is only temporary and things will normalise soon," one Japanese bank dealer said.
Overnight dollars rose to a high of 17.0 percent before settling at 14.0 percent in late morning. Overnight swap was at -0.05/par and tom/next at -0.10/-0.05 points.
Dealers said a combination of factors caused the short-dated swaps to fall while short-term money was on the rise and dollar liquidity was tight.

One dealer said local operators who sold dollars previously had to collect the U.S. currency now while on the other hand they were also doing arbitrage with the swap market to enjoy high overnight rates in the money market.
"This seem to have pushed overnight dollars higher as they also need dollars to buy swaps," the dealer said.
He said the cheap short-dated swaps could have resulted from operators' selling of swaps they had purchased earlier but reloaded to the market because they could not mobilise dollars.
"Besides, offshore players were also over supplied with swaps. Before they bought dollars they had gone long in swaps."
The central bank continued with its recent policy of keeping short-term money relatively expensive and remained absent from the short-term securities market (SBPUs).

The bank offered one-to-three-day bilateral SBIs at 14.0 percent, one-week at 10.0 percent, two-week at 10.5 percent, one-month at 11.125 percent, three at 11.0, six at 11.625 and one-year at 12.25 percent.
One-month money was traded at 16.75/17.00 percent and three-month money at 16.5/17.0 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Monday was 16.58 percent compared with 16.13 percent last Friday.
